source_text.body:
Open every AI story from a news homepage in tabs
A Comet user had it open The Verge's homepage and open all AI stories in new tabs, and also reported it handling email, LinkedIn messages and Reddit posts.
·
Jan 1, 2025
Done with
PC
Perplexity Comet
What they did
Commenters describe Comet as a browser agent that can act directly on logged-in web pages. In the example tied to this entry, one user told it to go to The Verge homepage and open every AI story in new tabs; elsewhere in the same thread, users say it could fill search fields on sites like LinkedIn, search Gmail, send a LinkedIn message, and reply on Reddit.
How it went
The reported result was that it did open AI stories from The Verge in separate tabs, and users also reported it working for email, LinkedIn messages, and Reddit comments. The thread also shows limits: one user said movie-ticket booking failed, and another found some document and spreadsheet tasks slower or unreliable.
Worth knowing
The main catch in the thread is inconsistency: several users said it works best on web UIs, but some tasks took longer than doing them manually or broke partway through.
Try it yourself
with
Perplexity Comet
Copy prompt
Open [news site homepage URL] and find every story about [topic, e.g. AI] currently on the page. Open each one in its own new tab, skipping duplicates, videos, and sponsored posts. When done, tell me how many tabs you opened and list the headlines in the order of the tabs.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/perplexity_ai/comments/1m6eh1s/ive_got_comet-never-use-itshould-i-and-what-for
